reason: The cited evidence supports the chemical similarity of Zr and Hf (E2) and that Ti or Zr addition decreases density (E3), but it does not provide direct evidence that fully substituting Hf with Zr maintains a single-phase solid solution or preserves strength at ~1000 °C; E2 even suggests removing Hf led to a reduced system, not a direct substitution.
premises: Zr and Hf have similar atomic size and chemical behavior
Replacing Hf with Zr reduces density due to lower atomic mass of Zr
The substitution maintains a single-phase solid solution
The resulting alloy retains high strength at room and elevated temperatures (~1000 °C)
